# Bibliographic linkage with displaced fields

Development question: can field-to-record containment recover a citation when an author name, venue or year has been appended to its title? A four-by-four field similarity matrix captures a displacement into a single other field. A field-to-whole-record feature can also capture a field whose tokens are distributed across several destination fields. The scientific question differs from the Tate alert audit.

Use the authors' dirty DBLP–ACM and DBLP–Google Scholar train and validation files. The input comprises the two serialized four-field records. Unit is a labeled candidate pair, and the primary metric is positive-class F1. Fit IDF and each classifier on 80% of the published training candidate pairs by a stable hash of the pair text. Select a decision threshold maximizing F1 on the other training pairs, using the highest threshold on ties. Screen once on both official validation sets. All models use the same fixed histogram gradient booster. Compare flattened text alone, same-field features plus flattened text, the full field-pair matrix plus flattened text, and field-to-record features plus flattened text. Candidate combines the matrix and field-to-record features. An advance requires at least one absolute F1 point beyond each comparator on both validation releases. A passing screen would still require a sealed comparison with Ditto and strong published specialist alternatives. A failed screen leaves the official test available for a separately motivated, prospectively frozen study.

This exploratory screen has no external registration. Token containment, field aggregation and similarity matrices are established matching operations. This experiment tests their incremental value under realistic competitor features. Scores on these validation pairs cannot establish a novel entity-matching architecture, performance on unseen works, or effectiveness for historical museum citations.
